stories.headline: Riyadh Airport Partly Reopens as Houthi Attacks Go On
stories.what_happened: Saudi Arabia reopened two terminals at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Sunday 25 October, about two weeks after attacks shut it. The same day, Saudi forces said they stopped missiles and drones fired by Yemen's Houthis.
stories.why_it_matters: The airport is the main gateway to Saudi Arabia's capital, and the attacks are part of a wider conflict that is pushing up oil prices around the world.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia reopened two terminals at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, 25 October 2026.
Terminal 1 handles domestic flights and Terminal 2 handles international flights.
The airport had been shut for about two weeks after strikes earlier in October.
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh and destroyed a drone aimed at the capital.
The coalition reported intercepting ten ballistic missiles aimed at the southern region.
The Houthis' spokesman described the airport as unsafe and said it remained a military target.
Saudi Arabia said it intercepted missiles and drones from the Iran-backed Houthis.
Emirates said flights to Riyadh and Dammam are due to resume on November 8.

stories.headline: Serbia Votes as Students Challenge Vucic
stories.what_happened: Serbia held a snap parliamentary election on 25 October. A list of candidates backed by a student protest movement challenged the ruling party of longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic, who resigned as president in September to run for prime minister.
stories.why_it_matters: It is the biggest challenge to Vucic's rule in more than a decade, and it shows how a protest movement can try to change a government at the ballot box.

key_facts.fact: Serbians voted in a parliamentary election on 25 October 2026.
A student protest movement wants to oust longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic.
Vucic resigned the presidency in September to run for prime minister.
The protests began after the 2024 collapse of a canopy at a newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.
The student list has 250 candidates for the 250-seat parliament; many are academics or political outsiders running on an anti-corruption platform.
Polls closed at 8pm local time, and first indications of results were expected about two hours later.
An Ipsos poll published on Thursday suggested Vucic's SNS party would win 47 percent of the vote to the students' 40 percent, while other polls put the students ahead.
The student list is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, with candidates such as professors, actors and farmers.
Reuters called the vote the biggest challenge to Vucic's rule for more than a decade.
Early turnout was strong, with long lines in front of polling stations.
The state election commission was not expected to release the official tally before Monday.
Lists generally need at least 3 percent of the vote to enter parliament.
The election followed almost two years of student-led protests over alleged corruption and authoritarianism.
An analyst expected the result to be very tight.

stories.why_it_matters: Higher oil prices make petrol, diesel and many goods cost more for families around the world.

US West Texas Intermediate crude added 3.8% to settle at $103.27 a barrel.
Brent rose 6.2% for the week, its third straight weekly gain.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and a reported UAE oil spill added to supply worries.
Traders were pricing in renewed US strikes on Iran.
Brent hit a six-month high above $116 a barrel as Houthi strikes fuelled supply fears.

stories.headline: Kim Jong Un Crosses a New Bridge Into China
stories.what_happened: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday 24 October, crossing the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge. He was met by senior Chinese official Wang Huning and returned home the same day.
stories.why_it_matters: China is by far North Korea's biggest trading partner, and the bridge is meant to carry much more trade between them, though some worry it could help North Korea get around international sanctions.

key_facts.fact: Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, 24 October 2026, crossing the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge.
Kim was accompanied by Wang Huning, China's fourth-highest-ranked official, who conveyed greetings from Xi Jinping.
Kim toured a Dandong automobile factory and paid tribute to Chinese soldiers at a Korean War memorial.
The 3 km bridge opened this month after a long delay.
China accounts for about 95% of North Korea's total official trade.
Some worry the bridge will help North Korea, the world's most-sanctioned country, evade bans on exports of its raw materials and other goods.
The bridge is expected to carry heavy equipment, raw materials and energy products, with two-way traffic around the clock.
Kim Jong Un visited China to inaugurate a new cross-border bridge.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab Heads for India's East Coast
stories.what_happened: A depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to grow into Cyclone Arnab and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam around the morning of 28 October. Odisha has closed schools in five southern districts and both states have readied rescue teams.
stories.why_it_matters: Early warnings, shelters and rescue teams ready in advance are how India now keeps people safe when big storms hit.

key_facts.fact: The India Meteorological Department expects the system to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm by the forenoon of October 28.
At landfall the storm is expected to have maximum sustained winds of 115-125 kmph, gusting to 140 kmph.
Heavy to very heavy rain is forecast over coastal Andhra Pradesh from October 27 to October 29.
A depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to turn into Cyclone Arnab, with landfall expected in Andhra Pradesh on October 28.
The IMD issued a red alert in Odisha ahead of Cyclone Arnab.
Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres will stay closed in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts of Odisha on October 28 and 29.
Odisha mobilised around 60 ODRAF teams, 17 NDRF teams and 225 Fire Services teams on alert.
Andhra Pradesh kept 25,000 electric poles and other materials ready for emergencies.

stories.headline: US Birth Rate Falls to a Record Low
stories.what_happened: A report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention shows the US birth rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded in 2025, down about 1% from 2024. Birth rates fell most among women in their twenties and teens, but rose a little among women over 30.
stories.why_it_matters: How many babies are born shapes a country's future: how many schools it needs, how many workers it will have and who will pay for care for older people.

key_facts.fact: The US birth rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded, according to a report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
The general fertility rate dropped 1% in 2025, continuing a two-decade trend toward fewer children.
The birth rate for women aged 20 to 24 fell 6%.
The birth rate for teens fell by about 7%.
Birth rates rose among older women, aged 30 to 45.
There were about 3.6 million births in 2025, a rate of roughly 53 per 1,000 women of reproductive age.
The 2025 rate is nearly 20% below the rate two decades ago.

stories.headline: Millions More Americans Vote Early
stories.what_happened: More than 18 million Americans had voted early by mail or in person by Thursday 22 October, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab, ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. NBC News's tracker later counted more than 27.8 million early votes.
stories.why_it_matters: The midterms decide who controls Congress, and early votes show how many people are taking part.

key_facts.fact: More than 18 million Americans had cast their votes early, by mail or in person, by Thursday, according to the Election Lab count cited by ABC News.
Democrats make up a much larger share of the early ballots cast so far, ABC News found, though early votes are only one piece of the puzzle.
NBC News's tracker showed 27,878,423 mail-in and early in-person votes cast nationally.

stories.headline: US Embassies in the Middle East Tighten Security
stories.what_happened: American embassies in the Middle East went on alert over warnings of Iranian plots, after the US ordered non-emergency government staff to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks worsened.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows how the conflict with Iran reaches Americans working abroad.

key_facts.fact: American embassies tightened security as warnings of Iranian threats intensified ahead of the US midterm elections.
The US ordered non-emergency government staff out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks worsened.
The administration has said it will hold off on renewed strikes on Iran until after the election.

stories.headline: Tiny Snakes Roll Like Wheels to Escape
stories.what_happened: Scientists at Toho University in Japan filmed dwarf reedsnakes from Southeast Asia and found they escape danger by rolling, reaching about four times their usual slithering speed. Their heads stay steady while the rest of the body swings round.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows animals can move in ways nobody expected, and studying how could help engineers design rolling robots.

key_facts.fact: Dwarf reedsnakes reached peak speeds of 1.72 to 3.69 metres per second while rolling, about four times their peak speed during normal side-to-side slithering.
The study was published in Current Biology by Yosuke Kojima and colleagues at Toho University.
While the rear of the body rotates, the head stays aligned with the direction of travel at a fairly constant height, which may help the snakes stay in control.
The snakes swing an arched section of body down past the head, a move the researchers call a stroke.
The snakes could stay on a racetrack only 20 centimetres wide while rolling.
The snakes cartwheel away from danger at more than 12 feet per second.

stories.headline: Brewers Come From Behind to Lead the World Series 2-0
stories.what_happened: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 in Game 2 of the World Series on Saturday 24 October, after the Rays scored four runs in the first inning. Milwaukee now leads the series 2-0.
stories.why_it_matters: The World Series decides baseball's champion; Milwaukee needs two more wins to take the title.

key_facts.fact: The Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 in Game 2 of the World Series on Saturday, October 24, at American Family Field, taking a 2-0 series lead.
Tampa Bay scored four runs in the first inning; Liam Hicks hit a home run for a 4-0 lead.
Sal Frelick's home run in the sixth inning tied the game at 4-4.
Cooper Pratt's single in the seventh inning brought Brice Turang home and gave the Brewers their first lead of the game.
The teams next meet at Tropicana Field for Game 3 on Monday.
Milwaukee needs two more victories to take the title.
